title: Interactive Job Runtime Refactor
description:
Master ticket for the interactivity-first refactor of the whole repo (excluding ./compose).

Coordinated by Claude Opus 5 (high effort) in the main chat; work packets executed by Sonnet 5 agent fleets; read-only reconnaissance by Haiku 4.5 fleets. (The ticket `llm` vocabulary predates these model ids, so it is left unset rather than recorded incorrectly.)

Governing rule: No interactive operation is a function call that runs until the operation is finished. Every interactive operation is a persistent state machine whose individual step is bounded, cancellable, observable, and preview-producing.

Targets:
- One process-wide worker scheduler (cpu_worker_count = max(1, N-1)); UI thread reserved and enqueue-only; no nested/subsystem CPU pools.
- 8 ms hard ceiling for any UI callback or worker step (normal steps 0.5-2 ms). Logical operations may last seconds but must yield and publish intermediate state continuously.
- Universal resumable job protocol (InteractiveJob::step -> StepOutcome) with operation ids, generations, checkpoints, cancellation, preview overlays, and progress-as-data streams.
- Every complex simulation (Puzzle fill, WFC, FEM, Energy) becomes composable resumable jobs previewing results in realtime (candidates/collisions, tested slots/propagation, mesh/assembly/residual/displacement, warmup/timestep/zone).
- Determinism under parallelism: same snapshot + inputs + seed => identical result at any worker count.
- Zero external dependencies across runtime AND build/test/tooling. Owned WASM interpreter replaces wasmtime+wit-bindgen. Owned event-log store replaces rusqlite/sqlx/neo4rs.

Executed in 11 phases (0-10), each with its own child ticket, dispatched as parallel agent fleets. This master ticket holds the plan, inventories, and the gate dashboard.

Baseline commit: 95b8688ee2f62f4056b6403c282bf0c76172c37c. Host: 10 logical cores.
